intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights while warming up with hot cocoa.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. The surreal volcanic lava field backdrop makes this one of Iceland's most iconic and relaxing experiences, especially magical under the northern lights in winter.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Swim in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the old city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, colorful harbor, and local fish markets while learning about Norse mythology and modern Icelandic culture.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across the stunning Vatnajökull glacier, Europe's largest ice cap, with a certified glacier guide. Descend into a breathtaking natural ice cave glowing in shades of blue and crystal. This thrilling adventure combines physical activity with awe-inspiring natural beauty and is a must-do for any Iceland visitor.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and baggage claim, then take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Before sleeping, step outside to scan the sky for northern lights — January skies in Iceland offer excellent aurora viewing opportunities.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the Keflavik Airport cafeteria or a snack from a vending machine upon arrival — keep it simple tonight

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency or withdraw ISK from an ATM at the airport. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for affordable data. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) to track aurora forecasts throughout your trip. January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C — dress in warm layers.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a slow morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Walk along the beachfront to get oriented with your surroundings and take in the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery. The black sand and winter light make for stunning free photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Reykjavik on foot — a completely free activity. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior free, tower viewing approx. 1,000 ISK), stroll Laugavegur shopping street, and visit the Sun Voyager sculpture on the waterfront. Pop into local supermarkets like Bonus or Kronan to stock up on budget groceries for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool (approx. 1,000 ISK entry). Soak in the hot pots as darkness falls — a perfect budget alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Afterward, check the aurora forecast and head to a dark spot near the resort for northern lights hunting.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — pick up oatmeal, yogurt, and fruit from Bonus supermarket
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand in Reykjavik — Iceland's most famous hot dog for under 500 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or soup at the resort using groceries from Bonus — budget approx. 800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means only 4-5 hours of daylight, so plan outdoor sightseeing during midday hours (roughly 11:00–15:30). Nights are long, which is excellent for northern lights viewing. Aurora forecast apps: Vedur.is and Space Weather app are your best tools.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to the Golden Circle — one of Iceland's most iconic free-to-access routes. Start at Þingvellir National Park (free entry), a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá canyon and see the Öxará River. Allow 2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area (free entry). Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting water 20-30 meters high. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls. In winter, it may be partially frozen, making it even more spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by late afternoon before full darkness. Stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir on the way back if budget allows (approx. 3,000 ISK) — a natural hot spring pool that is far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. Back at the resort, check aurora forecasts and go northern lights hunting near the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — eggs and toast
meals.lunch: Pack a packed lunch from the resort — sandwiches and thermos of hot coffee or soup to enjoy at Geysir
meals.dinner: Skúbb or Hlöllabátar sandwich shop in Reykjavik — budget meal under 1,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for the Golden Circle is most cost-effective when split among travel companions — try Sad Cars or Geysir Car Rental for budget options. Alternatively, take a budget group tour from BSÍ bus terminal (approx. 7,000-9,000 ISK). Roads may be icy — drive carefully and check road conditions at road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walk around Reykjavik's colorful old town (Gamla Reykjavík). Visit the Tjörnin lake in the city center — often partially frozen in January and home to numerous bird species. Walk through the old harbor area and admire the Harpa Concert Hall exterior (free to enter the lobby).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (approx. 2,000 ISK) for a deep dive into Viking history and Icelandic culture — well worth the budget spend. Alternatively, the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) is nearby and equally fascinating. Browse the flea market at Kolaportið (open weekends, free entry) if it falls on a weekend.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost aurora hunting walk organized by the city, or simply drive to the Grótta lighthouse at the tip of the Seltjarnarnes peninsula — one of the best free northern lights viewing spots near Reykjavik with minimal light pollution. Bundle up and bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — yogurt with granola and fruit
meals.lunch: Grab a bowl of Icelandic lamb soup (Kjötsúpa) at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja for approx. 1,800 ISK — a hearty, traditional budget meal
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort — rice and canned fish stew, approx. 700 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Grótta lighthouse area is only a 20-minute walk from central Reykjavik. Check tide schedules as the causeway to the lighthouse can flood at high tide. January aurora activity is statistically high — KP index of 3 or above gives good viewing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula — easily accessible from the resort by bus or car. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) where you can walk a small bridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Explore the dramatic lava fields of the peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gunnuhver hot spring area (free) — one of Iceland's most powerful geothermal areas with massive steam vents and mud pools. Also explore the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse) and the dramatic coastal cliffs. The entire peninsula feels otherworldly in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. If budget allows, treat yourself to the Blue Lagoon (book well in advance, from 8,000 ISK for the Comfort package) — though the Secret Lagoon visited earlier is the budget alternative. Otherwise, enjoy Laugardalslaug again (1,000 ISK) and then aurora hunt from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — oatmeal with honey and banana
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the resort for the Reykjanes Peninsula — save money by eating outdoors
meals.dinner: Noodle Station in Reykjavik — a beloved budget restaurant offering large bowls of noodle soup from approx. 1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has been volcanically active in recent years — check local news and SafeTravel.is for any volcanic activity updates before visiting. The area around Svartsengi and Grindavík may have access restrictions. Always have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and local exploration. Sleep in after any late-night aurora hunting. Walk along the beachfront near the Aegean Bliss Resort and enjoy the dramatic winter coastal scenery. Collect volcanic rocks and black sand (do not remove from protected areas). Practice aurora photography techniques for the coming nights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Perlan Museum (exterior and free viewing deck — the paid museum is approx. 3,000 ISK but optional). The building sits atop Öskjuhlíð hill with panoramic views of Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains and sea. Walk through the surrounding Öskjuhlíð woodland trails for free.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget northern lights tour departing from Reykjavik (approx. 5,000-7,000 ISK) — guides know the best dark spots and will chase clear skies. Many tours offer a free second attempt if no lights are seen. This is one of the best value investments of the trip for aurora hunters.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — scrambled eggs and toast
meals.lunch: Bonus supermarket ready-made sandwich or salad — under 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Mandi Restaurant in Reykjavik — affordable Middle Eastern food, shawarma wraps under 1,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Budget northern lights tours to look for: Arctic Adventures, Reykjavik Excursions, and Extreme Iceland all offer competitive pricing. Book online in advance for the best rates. Bring hand warmers, a warm hat, gloves, and waterproof outer layers for the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip along the South Coast — one of Iceland's most dramatic scenic drives. Depart early (around 9:00-9:30 to maximize daylight). First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free) — in summer you can walk behind it, but in winter the path may be icy and closed. Still spectacular from the front.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall (free) — a massive 60-meter-wide, 25-meter-tall curtain of water. Climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views over the South Coast. Then drive to Reynisfjara black sand beach (free) near Vík — one of the world's most beautiful beaches with dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The South Coast drive offers excellent northern lights viewing away from city light pollution — pull over at any safe roadside area if the aurora appears. Return to the resort by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before departure — quick oatmeal and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial packed lunch — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and a thermos of hot soup for the road
meals.dinner: Stop at a local grill or gas station restaurant in Vík (Suður-Vík restaurant) for a budget meal around 2,000-2,500 ISK, or self-cater at the resort upon return

day_by_day.notes: WARNING: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay well above the waterline. Check road conditions at road.is before departure. The South Coast drive is approximately 180km from Reykjavik — allow a full day. A rental car is strongly recommended for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the long South Coast day. Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (free, though most plants are dormant in January — the setting is still peaceful) and the nearby Árbær Open Air Museum (approx. 1,800 ISK) showcasing traditional Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Elliðaárdalur valley — a beautiful free nature area within Reykjavik city limits. Walk along the Elliðaá river where Atlantic salmon run in summer. The valley has well-marked free hiking trails and feels surprisingly remote despite being in the city. Look for Arctic foxes and birds.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Laugardalslaug thermal pool again for a relaxing soak (1,000 ISK). The hot pots are particularly enjoyable on cold January evenings. Then return to the resort for aurora hunting — set an alarm for 23:00 and 01:00 to check the sky if cloud cover is variable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — full cooked breakfast with eggs, toast, and juice
meals.lunch: Gló restaurant in Reykjavik — healthy, affordable vegetarian and vegan options from approx. 1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort — homemade Icelandic lamb soup using ingredients from Bonus (approx. 1,000 ISK total)

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug also has a water slide and steam room included in the entry price. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees. The hot pot temperatures range from 36°C to 44°C — start in the cooler ones and work up. January aurora probability is high — KP index forecasts available at en.vedur.is/weather/forecasts/aurora.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus or drive to Þórsmörk (Thor's Valley) — only possible with a 4WD vehicle in winter due to river crossings. Alternatively, explore the Hveragerði geothermal town (approx. 45 minutes from Reykjavik by bus). Walk the Reykjadalur hot spring river trail (free) — a 3km hike to a natural hot river where you can bathe for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Reykjadalur hot river — bring a swimsuit and towel. The hike takes about 45-60 minutes each way through geothermal terrain with steaming vents, mud pools, and beautiful winter landscapes. The river is naturally warm (38-40°C in the best spots). This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hveragerði town and browse the local greenhouse culture (some offer affordable fresh vegetables and flowers). Take the bus back to Reykjavik and the resort. Check aurora forecast and do a late-night aurora hunt from a dark spot near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy after the hot river soak — sandwiches, thermos of hot tea, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Kaffi Krús in Hveragerði — a cozy local café with affordable soups and sandwiches under 1,500 ISK, or self-cater at the resort

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur trail can be slippery and icy in January — bring microspikes or traction devices for your boots. The trail is well-marked but can be challenging in poor weather. Check conditions before going. Bring a dry bag for your clothes while you soak. This is genuinely one of the best free experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of Reykjavik using a downloaded map or app. Cover the 101 Reykjavik district thoroughly — Austurvöllur square, Alþingishús (parliament building), Dómkirkjan cathedral, and the old harbor. Visit the free Reykjavik City Library and warm up with a book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition (approx. 2,900 ISK) — the world's largest exhibition of whale models, very educational and impressive. Alternatively, take a free walk around the Grandi harbor district, which has been redeveloped into a hip area with street art, the Reykjavik Maritime Museum exterior, and local fish market.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a budget-friendly Northern Lights boat tour from Reykjavik Old Harbor (approx. 5,500-7,000 ISK) — viewing aurora from the water with no light pollution is a magical experience. Tours last 2-3 hours and include hot chocolate. Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — yogurt parfait with granola
meals.lunch: Grandi Mathöll food hall in the harbor area — multiple vendors with affordable options from 1,200-2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the resort before the evening boat tour — simple pasta dish

day_by_day.notes: Northern lights boat tours are weather and sea-condition dependent. The tour operator will notify you of cancellations — most offer free rebooking. Dress in your absolute warmest layers for the boat — wind chill on the water is significant. Many operators provide overalls and blankets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2 hours from Reykjavik) — made famous by Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Drive or take a bus tour. Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park (free entry) and the dramatic glacier-capped volcano at its heart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Snæfellsnes coastline — visit the Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages (free), walk the dramatic lava arch formations, and see the Gatklettur arch rock. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) with its haunting shipwreck remains. The entire peninsula feels magical in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is far from city lights — if the aurora appears on the drive back, pull over safely and enjoy the show with the glacier and lava fields as a backdrop. This could be the best aurora moment of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before early departure
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial packed lunch — this is a long day trip with limited food options on the peninsula
meals.dinner: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar (if open in January) for fresh fish soup — approx. 1,800 ISK, or self-cater at the resort on return

day_by_day.notes: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 200km round trip from Reykjavik. A rental car is strongly recommended. Check road.is for road conditions — mountain roads on the peninsula can close in bad weather. Budget bus tours are available from Reykjavik (approx. 9,000-12,000 ISK) but a car offers more flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated hot springs and geothermal day. Start with a visit to Deildartunguhver — Europe's highest-flow hot spring (free to view, approx. 1.5 hours from Reykjavik). The massive boiling spring produces 180 liters of 100°C water per second — an incredible natural spectacle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krauma Geothermal Baths near Reykholt (approx. 3,500 ISK) — a beautiful, affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon fed directly by Deildartunguhver's water. Five outdoor pools of varying temperatures, a cold pool, and a relaxation room. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and equally stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik for your final full evening of aurora hunting. Visit Öskjuhlíð hill near Perlan for an elevated dark viewing spot. Alternatively, drive to Þingvellir National Park (40 minutes from Reykjavik) for the darkest skies near the capital — one of Iceland's premier aurora viewing locations. Stay out until midnight if the forecast is good.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — a good hearty breakfast before the day trip
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the road — save money for the Krauma entry fee
meals.dinner: Celebrate the penultimate evening with a slightly larger budget dinner — try Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbor for langoustine soup (approx. 1,500 ISK) — a beloved local institution

day_by_day.notes: Krauma Baths are much less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon and offer an equally authentic geothermal experience at roughly half the price. Booking in advance is recommended. The drive to Reykholt passes through beautiful Borgarfjörður valley — allow time to enjoy the scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take one last walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to the Icelandic coast. Visit a local bakery for a traditional Icelandic pastry (skúffukaka chocolate cake or kleina fried doughnut) and coffee — a sweet farewell treat under 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend remaining hours in Reykjavik. Pick up affordable souvenirs at Bonus supermarket (Icelandic chocolate, skyr, licorice) rather than tourist shops — save significant money. Visit any remaining sights on your list. Head to Keflavik Airport via Flybus (book return journey in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of northern lights, hot springs, dramatic landscapes, and Viking history. Review your aurora photos and geothermal experiences — you've completed a comprehensive budget Iceland itinerary.

meals.breakfast: Local Reykjavik bakery — Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur for fresh pastries and coffee under 1,200 ISK
meals.lunch: One final hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the perfect budget farewell to Iceland under 500 ISK
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Keflavik or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY TIPS: Total accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Daily food budget averaging 2,000-3,500 ISK using supermarket shopping and selective restaurant visits. Key paid experiences: Laugardalslaug (1,000 ISK x multiple visits), Golden Circle transport (7,000-9,000 ISK), Secret Lagoon (3,000 ISK), Northern Lights tour (5,500-7,000 ISK), Krauma Baths (3,500 ISK). Free highlights: Þingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss, Reynisfjara, Reykjadalur hot river, all waterfalls, all coastal walks. Always check road.is before driving and SafeTravel.is for safety updates.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Keep an eye on the sky tonight — January nights in Iceland are long and dark, making spontaneous northern lights sightings possible right from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the airport or a convenience store en route to the hotel (Nói Síríus or 10-11 stores are open late)

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means roughly 5 hours of daylight (around 11am–4pm). Temperatures average -1°C to 3°C. Pack warm layers. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) and Aurora Forecast app before leaving home — they will be your best friends this trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a short walk along the beachfront to get your bearings and breathe in the crisp Icelandic sea air. The dramatic winter coastline near the resort is stunning even in low light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 20–30 minutes from most coastal resort areas near Reykjavik). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, enjoy an in-water silica mud mask, and let the mineral-rich waters ease your jet lag. Book the Comfort package (~8,000–9,500 ISK) which includes a towel, one drink, and silica mud mask.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and rest. If the Aurora forecast shows KP index 3 or above, step outside or arrange a short drive away from any light sources for a chance at your first northern lights sighting. Check the Vedur app around 9pm–midnight.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fuel up with skyr (Icelandic yogurt), eggs, smoked salmon, and rye bread
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon has an in-water LAVA Restaurant bar — grab a light in-water snack (soup or a small plate, ~2,500–3,500 ISK) or eat before you go at a nearby petrol station café
meals.dinner: Dine at the resort restaurant or a nearby casual spot — try Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) or fish and chips at a local grill (~3,500–5,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in winter. Arrive 15 minutes early. Bring flip-flops. Condition your hair before entering as the silica can be drying.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from central Reykjavik (approximately 20–30 minutes from the resort). Explore the colorful streets of the capital, taste traditional Icelandic foods including skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), brennivín schnapps, pylsur (Icelandic hot dog), and fresh langoustine. Learn about Viking heritage and modern Icelandic culture. Tours typically run 10am–1pm.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, explore Reykjavik independently. Visit Hallgrímskirkja Church for panoramic city views from the tower (~1,000 ISK), stroll Laugavegur shopping street, and browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for local crafts and vintage finds. Pop into the National Museum of Iceland (~2,000 ISK) to deepen your Viking history knowledge.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour departing from Reykjavik. A small-group guided tour drives you away from the city's light pollution to optimal viewing locations. Tours typically depart 9pm–10pm and last 2–4 hours. Guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive to multiple locations if needed.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at Brauð & Co bakery in Reykjavik before the walking tour
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the food tour will keep you satisfied — supplement with an Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur, the famous hot dog stand (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Affordable and hearty pre-tour dinner at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — try the famous lobster soup (~2,500 ISK) or grilled fish skewers before heading out for the aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: Dress in your warmest layers for the evening aurora tour — standing outside in January can mean -5°C to -10°C with wind chill. Hand warmers are highly recommended. Most tour operators offer a free rebooking if aurora activity is too low on your chosen night.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late aurora tour. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast at the resort. If the previous night's tour was successful, use this morning to review photos and journal. If aurora was a miss, check tonight's forecast and consider rebooking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus to the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approximately 1.5 hours from Reykjavik). Iceland's oldest swimming pool (dating to 1891) is a wonderfully authentic and less commercialized alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Admission ~3,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner and monitor the aurora forecast. If conditions are favorable (KP 3+, clear skies), drive to a dark spot near the coast for independent aurora watching — the beachfront location of the resort may already offer decent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — skyr with berries, oatmeal, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a Reykjavik grocery store (Bónus or Krónan) before heading to Flúðir — sandwiches, fruit, and Skyr (~1,500–2,000 ISK total). There is a small café at Secret Lagoon for light snacks.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the resort if kitchen facilities are available, or dine at a local restaurant near the resort — try grilled Arctic char or pan-fried cod (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Flúðir takes you through beautiful Icelandic countryside. Road conditions in January can be icy — check road.is before every drive. Consider renting a 4WD vehicle for the trip if not already arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Golden Circle route independently. Start with Þingvellir National Park (Thingvellir) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the dramatic rift valley, visit the ancient Viking parliament site (Alþingi), and admire the frozen or partially frozen Öxará river. (~45 min from Reykjavik)
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, partially frozen in winter and absolutely breathtaking. (~1 hour between stops)
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop at a cozy restaurant in the Selfoss or Hveragerði area for dinner. If aurora forecast is strong tonight, pull over at any dark roadside area on the way back — the Golden Circle route away from towns offers excellent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to get on the road by 9–9:30am to maximize the limited daylight hours
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café near Strokkur — warm lamb soup, sandwiches, or fish dishes (~2,500–3,500 ISK). Alternatively, pack a lunch from a grocery store.
meals.dinner: Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant near Reykholt — a unique farm restaurant set inside a geothermal tomato greenhouse. Famous for tomato soup and tomato-based dishes (~4,500–6,000 ISK). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Daylight window is roughly 11am–4pm in January. Plan your outdoor sightseeing within this window. Gullfoss and Þingvellir are accessible with standard vehicles but dress extremely warmly — wind chill at waterfalls and open rift valleys is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend the morning relaxing at the resort. Use the time to charge camera batteries, back up photos, do laundry, and plan the second week of the trip. If the resort has a hot tub or pool, enjoy a morning soak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula (very close to the resort area if located near Keflavik) for a scenic afternoon drive. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (a small footbridge over the Mid-Atlantic Ridge), the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest), and the dramatic Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools and fumaroles. Entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Second attempt at a Northern Lights Guided Tour if the first was cloudy or if you want a different route. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at the resort with dinner and aurora watching from the beachfront if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Café at the Reykjanes area or a drive-through in Keflavik town — try Kaffi Duus for harbor views and fresh fish (~3,000–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or order in — try a traditional Icelandic meat soup (kjötsúpa) or a hearty fish stew to warm up after the cold afternoon

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically one of the most active areas in Iceland. In recent years it has seen volcanic eruptions — check current volcanic activity status at vedur.is before visiting the peninsula. Some areas may be restricted.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the South Coast drive. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — a stunning 60-meter waterfall you can walk behind (path may be icy/closed in January, check conditions). Nearby Skógafoss waterfall is equally dramatic and often has ice formations in winter. (~1.5–2 hours from Reykjavik)
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the most dramatic beaches in the world with basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks), powerful Atlantic waves, and jet-black volcanic sand. Exercise extreme caution — sneaker waves here are dangerous. Never turn your back on the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stay in or near Vík (book a guesthouse in advance, ~15,000–20,000 ISK/night for a mid-range option) or return to the resort (2.5-hour drive). If staying near Vík, the dark skies around Vík are exceptional for aurora viewing — some of Iceland's best.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure (~8:30am)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at Skógarfoss Café near the waterfall for soup and sandwiches (~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dine in Vík — try Sudur-Vík restaurant for Icelandic lamb and fish dishes (~4,500–6,500 ISK) or the Black Crust Pizzeria for a more casual option

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 5–6 hours total including stops, all within the limited daylight window. Start no later than 9am. Roads in this area can be challenging in January. Check road.is. The South Coast is one of Iceland's most scenic drives and absolutely worth the effort.

day_by_day.morning: If you stayed near Vík, drive further east toward Vatnajökull for the Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration. Depart by 8am to meet your guide near Skaftafell or Jökulsárlón. Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier — Vatnajökull. Your certified glacier guide will lead you safely across the icy terrain, explaining glacier formation and climate change impacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a stunning crystal-blue ice cave inside the glacier. Natural ice caves are only safely accessible in winter (November–March) when the ice is frozen solid. The electric blue ice walls are otherworldly and make for extraordinary photography. Tours typically last 3–4 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 30 minutes from the glacier base) — watch icebergs calve from the glacier and drift across the lagoon in the eerie blue twilight. Then visit Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash up on black volcanic sand. Begin the drive back toward the resort (approximately 4–5 hours) or overnight locally.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Vík guesthouse or a packed breakfast to eat in the car
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch — there are limited food options near the glacier. Hot soup in a thermos is highly recommended for warmth during the glacier hike.
meals.dinner: If driving back toward Reykjavik, stop in Kirkjubæjarklaustur (known as Klaustur) for dinner at Systrakaffi — a cozy local restaurant with lamb and fish dishes (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike and ice cave MUST be booked in advance through a certified guide company (e.g., Glacier Guides, Arctic Adventures, or Local Guide). Never attempt glacier hiking without a guide. Wear warm, waterproof layers. The ice cave tours are among the most memorable experiences in Iceland — this is a highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the resort if you overnighted in the south. Alternatively, if back at the resort, enjoy a slow morning. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús branch) — a fantastic mid-range cultural experience featuring Icelandic contemporary art and the iconic Erró permanent collection (~2,000 ISK). Located in the old harbor area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Old Harbour (Grandi) district of Reykjavik. Visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition (impressive life-size whale models, ~3,500 ISK), browse the Grandi Mathöll food hall for local snacks, and walk along the harbor watching fishing boats and seabirds. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking-age longhouse (~2,200 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Reykjavik. Explore the lively bar scene on Laugavegur and Austurstræti streets. For a culturally rich evening, check if Harpa Concert Hall has any performances — Icelandic Symphony Orchestra concerts are world-class and tickets start around 3,000–5,000 ISK.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a Reykjavik café — try Café Babalú for cozy atmosphere and great coffee
meals.lunch: Grandi Mathöll food hall at the Old Harbour — sample Icelandic street food including lobster rolls, lamb tacos, and freshly baked goods (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur restaurant — a celebrated mid-range restaurant serving modern takes on traditional Icelandic recipes like salt cod head, rye bread ice cream, and cured lamb (~6,000–8,000 ISK per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings in Reykjavik are lively. If you enjoy the nightlife scene, Icelanders typically start their evenings late (10pm–11pm). The city is very walkable and safe. Taxis and rideshares are available for the return to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Laugardalur Valley area of Reykjavik — home to the Laugardalslaug public swimming pool and hot pot complex. Swim with locals in the outdoor geothermal pools and hot tubs (~1,000 ISK). This is quintessential Icelandic culture — locals gather here daily to soak, chat, and relax regardless of weather. A must-do authentic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Hveragerði (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavik) — Iceland's 'hot spring town.' Walk the geothermal park in the town center where hot springs bubble up between houses. If conditions allow, hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River Trail (~3km each way) to a natural hot river where you can bathe in geothermally heated water flowing through a valley. Trail may be icy — use microspikes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing final full-week evening. Enjoy dinner at the resort, review your best photos, and check the aurora forecast for one more potential sighting. The beachfront location may offer a clear horizon for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Álafoss wool factory outlet café in Mosfellsbær (en route) or pack a lunch for the Reykjadalur hike — bring a thermos of hot chocolate for the trail
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner: grilled lamb chop or pan-seared Arctic char (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike to the hot river is one of Iceland's most unique experiences. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and a dry bag. The changing area at the river is basic (a small wooden screen). Water temperature varies along the river — find your perfect temperature spot. Allow 2–3 hours round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — one of Iceland's most diverse and dramatic landscapes (approximately 2 hours from Reykjavik). Start with Snæfellsjökull National Park, home to the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk around the Arnarstapi lava field coastal path with dramatic sea cliffs and arch formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the peninsula to Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, often called 'arrowhead mountain.' The nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall creates an iconic foreground for photography, especially in winter light. Explore the charming fishing village of Grundarfjörður for a coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward the resort. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is known as a prime aurora viewing location due to its distance from Reykjavik's light pollution. If aurora activity is forecast, stop on the peninsula's northern coast for viewing before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the 2-hour drive
meals.lunch: Arnarstapi village has a small café — try fresh fish soup or a lamb sandwich (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar (if still open in January — check ahead) is a beloved cliffside café with homemade cakes and soups, or dine back at the resort upon return

day_by_day.notes: This is another long driving day (~5–6 hours total). The Snæfellsnes Peninsula road is well-maintained but check conditions at road.is. The peninsula is sometimes called 'Iceland in Miniature' because it contains almost every type of Icelandic landscape — glaciers, lava fields, beaches, mountains, fishing villages, and bird cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed penultimate morning. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and begin packing non-essentials. Take a final long walk along the beachfront to soak in the atmosphere. Visit any local shops near the resort for last-minute souvenirs — look for Icelandic wool lopapeysa sweaters, lava salt, skyr, and locally made chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final hot spring experience — visit one of the lesser-known geothermal pools near the resort area. Options include Seljavallalaug (a remote pool near Skógar, though it requires a 15-minute hike in winter), or revisit Laugardalslaug in Reykjavik for a final local pool experience. Alternatively, book a relaxing massage or geothermal body treatment at a local spa.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — if you haven't had a clear sighting yet, tonight is your last chance. Book a final Northern Lights Guided Tour or self-drive to a dark location. The aurora season in January is at its peak — statistically, with 12 nights in Iceland, most visitors see the aurora at least once. Celebrate the trip with a special farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — savor it as one of the last
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Reykjavik café — try Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja for traditional Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smørrebrød style) and rye bread ice cream (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — one of Reykjavik's best mid-to-upscale restaurants specializing in Icelandic ingredients cooked over lava rocks. Try the lamb, lobster, or catch of the day (~7,000–10,000 ISK per person). Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: If you haven't seen the northern lights yet, don't despair — January KP activity can be unpredictable. Tonight's guided tour gives you the best final chance. Even if clouds prevent a sighting, the experience of standing in the Icelandic darkness listening to your guide discuss the aurora is memorable in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is typically 11am — confirm with the hotel). Enjoy one last resort breakfast. If time permits before heading to the airport, make a final stop at the Blue Lagoon for a farewell soak — it is located directly on the route between Reykjavik and Keflavik Airport, making it a perfect last activity. Book the early morning slot (7am or 8am) to allow plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Blue Lagoon visit, drive to the airport, and check-in/security. Browse the Duty Free at Keflavik Airport — excellent prices on Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), Icelandic chocolate, and cosmetics (including Blue Lagoon skincare products).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Iceland — the glowing auroras, steaming hot springs, glacial ice caves, dramatic waterfalls, and the unique warmth of Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go back for seconds on the skyr and smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon in-water bar or the LAVA Restaurant for a final geothermal meal (~2,500–4,000 ISK) or grab food at Keflavik Airport (Icelandic lamb soup is available airside)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight departure time and work backward to plan the Blue Lagoon visit. Most flights from Keflavik depart in the afternoon or evening — a morning Blue Lagoon slot works perfectly. Pre-book the Blue Lagoon slot for this morning as soon as your flight details are confirmed. Don't forget to pick up any checked luggage restrictions on Icelandic spirits from Duty Free.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights while warming up with hot cocoa.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. The surreal volcanic lava field backdrop makes this one of Iceland's most iconic and relaxing experiences, especially magical under the northern lights in winter.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Swim in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape at a fraction of the cost.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the old city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, colorful harbor, and local fish markets while learning about Norse mythology and modern Icelandic culture.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across the stunning Vatnajökull glacier, Europe's largest ice cap, with a certified glacier guide. Descend into a breathtaking natural ice cave glowing in shades of blue and crystal. This thrilling adventure combines physical activity with awe-inspiring natural beauty and is a must-do for any Iceland visitor.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome amenity — a glass of Icelandic schnapps and a warm bowl of traditional lamb soup prepared by the resort's chef. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: On board / pre-arrival
meals.lunch: On board / pre-arrival
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome supper at the resort: smoked Arctic char, skyr mousse, and warm rye bread served in your suite or at the resort's private dining lounge.

day_by_day.notes: Pack warm layers in your carry-on — January temperatures in Iceland hover between -3°C and 3°C. The resort will have a hot-water bottle, heated floors, and a wool blanket ready in your suite. Keep expectations light for Day 1; rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning to acclimate to the cold Icelandic air with a short beachfront stroll along the black-sand coastline, watching the dramatic winter sunrise (around 11:00 AM in January). The resort's spa offers a complimentary morning soak in its private geothermal pool to help reset your body clock.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 20 minutes from the resort by private transfer). Book the exclusive Retreat Spa package — enjoy the silica-rich milky-blue waters, an in-water massage, a silica mud mask treatment, and access to the private Retreat lagoon away from the general public. Spend 3–4 luxurious hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and dine at the resort's signature restaurant. Dress smartly for a candlelit dinner featuring a tasting menu of New Nordic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Skyr parfait with Icelandic berries, smoked salmon on rye, poached eggs, and fresh-pressed cloudberry juice.
meals.lunch: At the Blue Lagoon Retreat: Enjoy the exclusive in-lagoon refreshment service — sparkling water, algae smoothies, and light bites such as lobster bisque and artisan flatbreads.
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: 5-course New Nordic tasting menu featuring langoustine tartare, reindeer loin with crowberry jus, and skyr cheesecake with glacial ice cream.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa well in advance — slots are extremely limited. Bring a swimsuit; the resort can provide premium robes and slippers. January daylight is only about 5 hours, so the lagoon experience will likely transition beautifully from daylight to starlit skies.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a private guided Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Your expert local guide will lead you through the colorful streets of Iceland's capital — visiting Hallgrímskirkja Church, the old harbor district, and curated artisan shops. Taste traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), kleinur pastries, and craft beers at a boutique brewery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall (a stunning glass façade architectural marvel on the harbor), browse the galleries at the National Museum of Iceland, and stop at a high-end wool and design shop for premium Icelandic souvenirs (Lopapeysa sweaters, handcrafted jewelry).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour departs after dark (approximately 18:00). Join a small-group luxury tour in a heated 4x4 super-jeep, venturing away from Reykjavik's light pollution to the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Your guide will use real-time aurora forecasting tools to maximize sighting chances. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Icelandic pancakes with bilberry compote, cured lamb, and fresh-brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: During the food tour: Multiple tastings at curated stops. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Dill Restaurant (Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) — book ahead for the seasonal tasting menu.
meals.dinner: Pre-tour: A hearty early dinner at Grillið at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — panoramic city views and premium Icelandic lamb chops, lobster, and seasonal vegetables before departing for the aurora tour.

day_by_day.notes: Northern lights sightings depend on solar activity (KP index) and cloud cover — your guide will monitor conditions. January is statistically one of the best months for aurora viewing due to long dark nights. Dress in thermal layers; the resort concierge can provide premium outdoor gear if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at the resort. Take advantage of the resort's private geothermal pool at dawn, watching the faint winter light creep over the horizon. A personal trainer or yoga instructor can be arranged by the resort for an in-suite or poolside morning session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart by private vehicle for the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort). This is Iceland's oldest swimming pool, set amid bubbling hot springs and geysers in a remote, otherworldly landscape. The Secret Lagoon is far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon, offering an authentic, intimate geothermal experience. Soak for 2–3 hours surrounded by steaming vents and natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: On the return journey, stop at the Geysir geothermal area (if timing allows) to witness the famous Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes under the dark winter sky — a magical and dramatic sight. Return to the resort for a private dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Smoked trout with cream cheese on dark rye, granola with Icelandic honey, and a hot pot of Icelandic herbal tea.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic box prepared by the resort chef: Lobster sandwiches, artisan cheeses, Icelandic flatbread, and thermos of lamb broth — enjoyed near the Secret Lagoon.
meals.dinner: In-resort private dining: Chef's table experience — a curated 4-course meal with wine pairing, served in an intimate setting with views of the beachfront.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon water temperature is approximately 38–40°C year-round. Bring your swimsuit and a change of warm clothes. The drive through the Icelandic highlands in winter is stunning — keep a camera ready for snow-covered lava fields and frozen waterfalls.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (07:00) by private luxury 4x4 for the South Coast adventure. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most iconic cascades. In winter, it transforms into a frozen curtain of ice, and you can walk behind it (conditions permitting). Next stop: Skógafoss waterfall, equally dramatic and often adorned with ice crystals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, flanked by towering basalt columns and crashing North Atlantic waves. Explore the sea caves and photograph the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the ocean. Then visit the charming village of Vík for a warm break.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop for dinner in Selfoss (Iceland's largest town outside the capital) at a premium local restaurant. Arrive back at the resort by 21:00. Check aurora forecast and, if conditions are favorable, step outside the resort for a potential spontaneous northern lights sighting from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast box: Warm pastries, smoked salmon bagel, fresh fruit, and a thermos of coffee — to enjoy on the road.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Strondin Bistro & Bar in Vík or a premium packed lunch from the resort: Lamb stew in a thermos, cheese and charcuterie board, and Icelandic chocolates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant in Reykholt (book ahead): Dine inside a working tomato greenhouse — unique tomato-based menu with fresh pasta, soups, and homemade breads, paired with Icelandic craft beer or local wines.

day_by_day.notes: South Coast roads are well-maintained but can be icy in January. Your private driver will handle all navigation. Wear waterproof boots — sea spray at Reynisfjara can be intense. Never turn your back to the ocean at this beach; sneaker waves are notorious here.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Indulge in a full luxury spa treatment — choose from a hot stone massage, an algae body wrap, or a volcanic mud facial offered by the resort's wellness center. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's private sauna and steam room overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula, a UNESCO Global Geopark just minutes from the resort. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (Iceland's largest), and the historic Reykjanesviti lighthouse — Iceland's oldest. The landscape here is raw, volcanic, and utterly alien.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour — second attempt (or first if the previous tour was cloudy). Tonight's tour heads toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula direction for darker skies. Your luxury tour operator will have a heated base camp with warm drinks, blankets, and a telescope for stargazing between aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Eggs Benedict with smoked lamb, avocado on sourdough, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a skyr smoothie.
meals.lunch: At the resort or a light café lunch in Grindavík town: Fish and chips made with fresh Atlantic cod, creamy langoustine soup, and Icelandic butter.
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at the resort: Nordic comfort food — slow-braised short rib, root vegetable purée, and a warm Icelandic apple cake with vanilla skyr cream.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically very active — there have been recent volcanic eruptions in the area (2021–2024 eruption series). Check with local authorities and your guide for current conditions and access. The landscape of hardened lava fields is extraordinary regardless.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the famous Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates are visibly pulling apart. Walk along the Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's Viking parliament (Alþingi), established here in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur erupt in daylight, then proceed to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall — a two-tiered cascade plunging into a dramatic canyon, often partially frozen in January with ice formations of extraordinary beauty. Spend time photographing and absorbing this iconic Icelandic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via a scenic route. Tonight, enjoy a private in-suite dinner with a curated wine list and a personal chef preparing a bespoke meal based on your preferences — the ultimate luxury Iceland dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast: Warm porridge with Icelandic cream and blueberries, smoked duck breast, freshly baked Icelandic bread, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: At the Geysir Center or Gullfoss Café: Lamb soup with fresh bread — Iceland's quintessential comfort meal on a cold winter day.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner: Lobster thermidor, pan-seared Arctic char with beurre blanc, artisan cheese board, and a warm chocolate lava cake with glacial ice cream.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route but is magical in winter with far fewer crowds. Dress in your warmest layers — wind chill at Gullfoss can be extreme. Allow a full day; don't rush any of the three main stops.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to a full-day glacier adventure. Depart early by private luxury 4x4 for Vatnajökull National Park (approximately 4–4.5 hours from the resort). En route, stop at the stunning Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a surreal landscape of floating icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier, drifting slowly to the sea. In January, the lagoon is partially frozen and eerily beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the glacier for your Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration experience. Strap on crampons and a helmet, and follow your expert mountain guide across the surface of Vatnajökull — Europe's largest ice cap. Descend into a natural ice cave, where the walls glow electric blue and crystalline ice formations create an otherworldly cathedral. This is one of Iceland's most extraordinary experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey. Stop for dinner in the town of Kirkjubæjarklaustur. Arrive back at the resort late (approximately 22:00–23:00). If aurora conditions are favorable, your driver will alert you to stop along the deserted highway for a spontaneous sighting.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to-go: Energy bars, smoked salmon wraps, thermos of hot coffee and chocolate — prepared by the resort for the long drive.
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box from the resort: Hearty lamb stew in a thermos, artisan sandwiches, nuts, dried fruit, and Icelandic chocolate — consumed in the 4x4 or near the glacier.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur: A beloved local restaurant — try the Icelandic lamb fillet, Arctic char, and homemade desserts in a warm, cozy atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are only available in winter (November–March) when the ice is stable. Your guide will assess safety conditions on the day. Wear thermal base layers, fleece mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell. The resort can arrange premium cold-weather gear rental if needed. This is a physically moderate activity — no prior experience necessary.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day after yesterday's long glacier adventure. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning in the resort's wellness facilities — geothermal pool, sauna, hot tub, and massage. Request a deep-tissue sports massage to recover from the glacier hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort on foot or by private car. Visit the nearby fishing village of Grindavík — browse the Saltfish Museum, chat with local fishermen, and pick up premium Icelandic sea salt and dried fish as gifts. Alternatively, arrange a private horse-riding experience on an Icelandic horse through the volcanic lava fields (the resort can arrange this).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort bar (sunset around 16:30 in January). Then enjoy a premium dinner at the resort's restaurant with a focus on Icelandic seafood — the freshest catch from the North Atlantic, just miles from your table.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Full Icelandic spread — skyr, smoked meats, pickled herring, rye bread, soft-boiled eggs, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort: Lobster bisque, a fresh salad with Icelandic microgreens, and sourdough with cultured butter.
meals.dinner: Resort seafood dinner: Whole roasted langoustine, pan-fried halibut with lemon butter and capers, dill-cured salmon, and a dessert of Icelandic bilberry tart with whipped cream.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately relaxed day to recharge mid-trip. January can be physically demanding with cold temperatures and long drives. Use this day to do laundry, journal, review photos, and plan any last-minute additions to the itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private Snæfellsnes Peninsula day tour (approximately 2 hours from the resort). This remote peninsula is dominated by the Snæfellsjökull glacier-capped volcano — the setting for Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Visit the dramatic Arnarstapi sea cliffs and lava arch, and the picturesque fishing village of Grundarfjörður with views of the iconic Kirkjufell mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — walk along the lava tube of Vatnshellir cave (guided tour), visit the black pebble beach of Djúpalónssandur, and photograph the jagged Lóndrangar basalt sea stacks. The entire peninsula feels like a landscape from another world, especially under January's pale Arctic light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 20:00. Tonight, enjoy a private Northern Lights watch from the resort's beachfront terrace — the resort's concierge will have set up heated outdoor loungers, blankets, warm drinks, and a direct line to an aurora forecaster for a magical, intimate experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Freshly baked cinnamon rolls, skyr with mango, smoked trout scrambled eggs, and freshly brewed Icelandic coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hotel Búðir (one of Iceland's most romantic and remote hotels) on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — black church backdrop, stunning views, and an excellent menu of Icelandic lamb and seafood.
meals.dinner: Resort dinner: Wild mushroom risotto with Icelandic herbs, slow-roasted duck breast with lingonberry sauce, and a warm rhubarb crumble with vanilla skyr.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in Miniature' because it showcases almost every Icelandic landscape type in one compact area. The drive along the peninsula's northern coast is particularly scenic. Hotel Búðir lunch reservation should be made in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Reykjavik for a full cultural immersion day. Start with a visit to the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — a fascinating underground museum built around the remains of an actual Viking longhouse from 871 AD. Then visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) for a curated tour of Icelandic modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon shopping on Laugavegur Street — Reykjavik's premier shopping boulevard. Visit premium Icelandic design stores for handmade ceramics, Lopapeysa wool sweaters, and unique lava jewelry. Stop at the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for local character. Then visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church tower for panoramic views over the city and harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner in Reykjavik (even though departure is still two days away) — celebrate the trip at one of Iceland's finest restaurants. Return to the resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: Eggs royale with smoked salmon, Icelandic waffles with bilberry jam, and a fresh green smoothie.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik — a critically acclaimed restaurant serving elevated traditional Icelandic cuisine. Try the 'Whole Cod's Head' or the lamb neck — adventurous and extraordinary.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Óx (Reykjavik's most exclusive restaurant — only 12 seats, chef's counter experience): An extraordinary 20+ course tasting menu of hyper-local Icelandic ingredients. Book months in advance. This is the pinnacle of Icelandic fine dining.

day_by_day.notes: Óx restaurant requires reservations far in advance and is one of the most sought-after dining experiences in Iceland. If unavailable, Dill Restaurant (Michelin-starred) is an excellent alternative. Both offer unforgettable New Nordic cuisine experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Iceland. Begin with a private helicopter tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula and surrounding volcanic landscapes (arrange through the resort concierge) — soar over lava fields, geothermal vents, the Blue Lagoon from above, and the dramatic coastline. This 45–60 minute flight offers an unparalleled perspective on Iceland's raw geological power.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final afternoon of pure luxury. Enjoy one last soak in the resort's private geothermal pool, book a final spa treatment (a relaxing aromatherapy massage or a volcanic clay body treatment), and begin packing. Take a long, reflective beachfront walk as the Arctic sun sets around 16:30.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at the resort — a special farewell meal arranged by the resort team. Request a private dining setup on the beachfront terrace (weather permitting) or in a private dining room with a personalized menu. Toast to the journey with a bottle of premium Champagne or Icelandic craft spirits.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: A full celebration breakfast — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, freshly baked pastries, Icelandic cheese board, fresh fruit platter, and a Mimosa or freshly pressed juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort: Creamy lobster soup with crusty bread, a mixed greens salad with pickled beets and goat cheese, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Private farewell dinner at the resort: Chef's personalized 6-course tasting menu — highlights of the trip reimagined on a plate. Paired with an Icelandic wine and spirits flight. Dessert: Skyr panna cotta with glacial water caramel and edible gold.

day_by_day.notes: If the helicopter tour is unavailable due to weather, consider a private snowmobile tour on a nearby glacier or a private boat tour along the Reykjanes coastline as an alternative. Confirm luggage pickup and private transfer to the airport for the following day. Keep one warm outfit accessible for the airport journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Complete any final packing and check out of your suite. The resort's concierge will arrange a luxurious private transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 20–30 minutes away). Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium lounge access and duty-free shopping — pick up Icelandic schnapps (Brennivín), premium Icelandic chocolates, and Skyr products as final souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming geothermal pools, ancient glaciers, and the raw, primal beauty of the North Atlantic's most magical island.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — homeward bound.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: A full Icelandic spread — everything you loved over the past 13 days, one last time. Savor it slowly.
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or on board: Icelandic airport lounges offer a solid selection of local dishes — try the lamb soup one final time before departure.
meals.dinner: On board or at connecting airport.

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport has a good duty-free selection of Icelandic products — budget time for shopping before your gate. The Icelandair Saga Lounge offers comfortable seating, warm food, and drinks for premium travelers. Confirm your flight details with the airline 24 hours before departure. Keep all receipts for VAT refund claims (Iceland offers tax refunds on purchases over 6,000 ISK for tourists).
